works.description_zh: 投影播放布努埃尔和达利的《一条安达鲁狗》（Un Chien Andalou）片段；观众的影子走进电影，取代了拖着三角钢琴的那个角色。
works.idea_en: Visitors' shadows walk into a surrealist film and take over the lead role.
works.technique_zh: 把摄像头实时捕捉的剪影合成进预先分割好的电影画面中，让影子触发并推动场景中的关键时刻。
works.exercise_en: Pick a classic film clip, use camera silhouettes to 'put' classmates into the frame and trigger the next shot. Twist: the scene continues only when a shadow strikes the same pose as the original character.

works.title: Apparition (with Ars Electronica Futurelab)
works.description: Two dancers perform inside an interactive projection that is generated in real time from their movements, both on the backdrop and directly on their bodies.
works.idea_zh: 舞者动作实时生成投影，投在背景和身体上，身体与影像相互牵引
works.technique: Infrared camera tracking extracts the dancers' silhouettes and motion, feeding physics-based generative visuals that are projected back on the performers and the screen in real time.
works.exercise_zh: 用摄像头提取舞者轮廓，驱动粒子或弹簧网格实时投回舞者身上；变化：让影像“拒绝”舞者——轮廓靠近时图案向外逃开。

video.video_title: Apparition – Klaus Obermaier & Ars Electronica Futurelab (2004)

works.description_zh: 两位舞者在互动投影中表演，投影根据他们的动作实时生成，既投在背景上，也直接投在他们的身体上。
works.idea_en: Dancers' moves generate projections live on the backdrop and on their bodies, so body and image pull on each other.
works.technique_zh: 红外摄像头追踪提取舞者的剪影和动作，输入基于物理的生成式视觉系统，再实时投射回表演者身上和屏幕上。
works.exercise_en: Extract a dancer's outline with a camera and use it to drive particles or a spring mesh projected back onto the dancer in real time. Twist: make the image 'reject' the dancer, with patterns fleeing outward as the outline approaches.

works.title: Cause and Effect
works.description: Viewers' silhouettes are recorded as they bump into the shadow-recordings of previous visitors; replays show only the recorded movements, so reactions look like autonomous gestures.
works.idea_zh: 你的动作被录下来，与前人的影子互相推挤，形成跨时间的因果链
works.technique: Silhouette clips recorded from a camera are placed on sliding tiles whose positions are displaced by live shadows, chaining recordings of different visitors together.
works.exercise_zh: 录下每位同学的剪影片段并排成一排，让下一位的影子推动前面的片段滑动；变化：把推挤的顺序变成一条可回放的“多米诺”时间线。

video.video_title: Cause and Effect (2004) by Scott Snibbe

works.description_zh: 观众的剪影在撞上此前观众的影子录像时被记录下来；回放时只显示录下的动作，因此那些反应看起来像是自发的手势。
works.idea_en: Your movements are recorded and jostle with the shadows of earlier visitors, forming a chain of cause and effect across time.
works.technique_zh: 摄像头录下的剪影片段放在可滑动的格子上，格子的位置会被实时影子推移，从而把不同观众的录像串联起来。
works.exercise_en: Record a silhouette clip of each classmate, line them up in a row, and let the next person's shadow push the earlier clips along. Twist: turn the order of pushes into a replayable 'domino' timeline.

works.title: Untitled 5 (External Measures series)
works.description: A projected 'living painting' where visitors' movements leave soft, overlapping painterly marks that respond to how long and how fast people stay.
works.idea_zh: 人的停留与移动在墙上留下会生长的绘画笔触
works.technique: Camera-tracked body positions and motion history drive generative brush-stroke systems that accumulate and decay over time.
works.exercise_zh: 用摄像头运动检测驱动生成式笔刷，在投影上留下随停留时间变粗的笔触；变化：只有两个人靠近时才会出现连接两人的线条。

video.video_title: Camille Utterback - Untitled 5

works.description_zh: 一幅投影出来的“活的绘画”：观众的动作留下柔和、相互交叠的绘画笔触，并会根据人停留的时长和移动的速度作出回应。
works.idea_en: People's pauses and movements leave growing brushstrokes on the wall.
works.technique_zh: 摄像头追踪的身体位置和运动历史驱动生成式笔触系统，笔触随时间累积并逐渐衰减。
works.exercise_en: Drive a generative brush with camera motion detection, leaving strokes on the projection that thicken the longer someone stays. Twist: a line connecting two people appears only when they come close to each other.

works.title: Compliant
works.description: A soft rectangle of projected light behaves like a rubber sheet: visitors' shadows push, dent and chase it around the wall.
works.idea_zh: 让屏幕像橡皮膜一样被人的影子推开、挤扁
works.technique: The shadow silhouette from a camera is used as a collision boundary for a spring-mesh (soft-body) simulation of the projected rectangle.
works.exercise_zh: 在p5.js里做一块弹簧网格方块，用摄像头人影轮廓当作碰撞体去推它并投影出来；变化：让方块被挤压时发出音调随形变变化的声音。

video.video_title: Compliant (2003) by Scott Snibbe

works.description_zh: 一块柔软的投影光矩形像橡皮膜一样：观众的影子可以推它、把它压出凹陷，还能追着它在墙上跑。
works.idea_en: Make the screen behave like a rubber sheet that people's shadows push and squash.
works.technique_zh: 把摄像头得到的影子剪影作为碰撞边界，用于投影矩形的弹簧网格（软体）模拟。
works.exercise_en: Build a spring-mesh square in p5.js, use the camera silhouette of a person as a collider to push it, and project the result. Twist: make the square emit a tone that changes pitch with its deformation when squeezed.

works.title: Frequency and Volume (Relational Architecture 9)
works.description: Visitors' shadows on a wall tune a radio: the position of the shadow selects a frequency and its size sets the volume, making the invisible airwaves audible and contested.
works.idea_zh: 用影子在墙上“调台”，收听城市里看不见的电波
works.technique: A camera tracks shadow position and size on the wall and maps them to frequency and volume of an array of computer-controlled radio receivers.
works.exercise_zh: 用摄像头检测墙上影子的水平位置控制音频播放的片段、大小控制音量；变化：让多个影子重叠时声音混合或互相干扰。

video.video_title: rafael lozano-hemmer: frequency and volume

works.description_zh: 观众投在墙上的影子可以调收音机：影子的位置选择频率，影子的大小决定音量，让看不见的电波变得可以听见，也变得可以争夺。
works.idea_en: Tune a radio with your shadow on the wall to hear the city's invisible airwaves.
works.technique_zh: 摄像头追踪墙上影子的位置和大小，并把它们映射为一组计算机控制的无线电接收器的频率和音量。
works.exercise_en: Use a camera to detect a shadow on the wall, with its horizontal position choosing which audio clip plays and its size setting the volume. Twist: when several shadows overlap, their sounds mix or interfere with each other.

works.title: Deep Walls
works.description: A projected wall of sixteen small cupboards: when someone walks into the beam their shadow is recorded, then replayed forever in one of the cupboards as a looping shadow-film of past visitors.
works.idea_zh: 把路过的人影录下来，放进墙上的“影子橱柜”永远循环播放
works.technique: A camera segments the viewer's silhouette against the projection, records it while someone is in frame, and drops the clip into a grid cell that loops once the space is empty.
works.exercise_zh: 用摄像头抠出人影剪影、录成几秒循环，再拼成网格投影；变化：每个格子只保留某一种动作（如挥手或跳），由简单规则判断放入哪一格。

video.video_title: Deep Walls (2002) by Scott Snibbe

works.description_zh: 墙上投影出十六个小橱柜：有人走进光束时，他的影子会被录下，随后在某个橱柜里永远循环播放，成为一段往昔访客的影子电影。
works.idea_en: Record passing shadows and keep them looping forever in 'shadow cupboards' on the wall.
works.technique_zh: 摄像头以投影为背景分割出观众的剪影，在有人入画时进行录制，并在空间变空后把片段放进网格中的一个格子里循环播放。
works.exercise_en: Use a camera to cut out people's silhouettes, record them as loops a few seconds long, and assemble them into a projected grid. Twist: each cell keeps only one kind of action (such as waving or jumping), with a simple rule deciding which cell a clip goes into.

works.title: Liquid Time Series
works.description: A viewer's movement fragments a pre-recorded street video: the closer they step to the projection screen, the deeper that part of the image slides into the past.
works.idea_zh: 你离屏幕越近，那一块画面就越退回到过去
works.technique: A camera measures each viewer's position and distance, and a slit-scan-style buffer picks older frames for image regions nearest to the viewer.
works.exercise_zh: 把一段视频存成帧缓冲，用摄像头检测人的位置，人所在的竖条显示更早的帧；变化：用手机距离传感或声音大小控制“回到过去”的深度。

video.video_title: Camille Utterback - Liquid Time Series - Tokyo and New York

works.description_zh: 观众的移动会把一段预先录制的街景视频打碎：他们离投影屏越近，那一部分画面就越深地滑回过去。
works.idea_en: The closer you get to the screen, the further that patch of the picture slips back into the past.
works.technique_zh: 摄像头测量每位观众的位置和距离，用类似狭缝扫描的缓冲区为离观众最近的图像区域选取更早的帧。
works.exercise_en: Store a video as a frame buffer, detect a person's position with a camera, and show earlier frames in the vertical strip where they stand. Twist: use the phone's proximity sensor or sound volume to control how far back into the past it goes.

works.title: Shadow (Screen Series)
works.description: A plain rectangle of projected light; viewers cast ordinary shadows, but after they step away their shadow keeps moving on the screen, repeating their gestures a moment later.
works.idea_zh: 你离开了，你的影子却留下来重复你刚才的动作
works.technique: A camera captures the viewer's shadow silhouette and the system re-projects the delayed silhouette sequence onto the same screen once the live shadow disappears.
works.exercise_zh: 用网页摄像头做背景差分得到人影，加入3秒延迟后投回墙上；变化：让延迟影子逐渐变淡并反向播放。

video.video_title: Shadow (2002) by Scott Snibbe

works.description_zh: 一块简单的投影光矩形；观众投下的起初只是普通的影子，但当他们走开后，影子仍在屏幕上移动，片刻之后重复他们刚才的动作。
works.idea_en: You have left, but your shadow stays behind and repeats what you just did.
works.technique_zh: 摄像头捕捉观众的影子剪影，当实时影子消失后，系统把延迟的剪影序列重新投射到同一块屏幕上。
works.exercise_en: Use background differencing on a webcam feed to get a person's shadow, and project it back onto the wall with a 3-second delay. Twist: make the delayed shadow gradually fade and play in reverse.

works.title: SmartSkin
works.description: A table surface senses several hands and fingers at once, even hovering just above it, so people can knead, spread and push projected shapes with both hands.
works.description_zh: 桌面能同时感应多只手、多根手指，甚至能感应悬停在表面上方的手，人们可以用双手揉、拉、推动投影出来的图形。
works.idea_en: Make any surface feel your whole hands, not just one pointer.
works.idea_zh: 让任何表面都能感知整只手，而不只是一个光标。
works.technique: A grid of transmitter and receiver electrodes under the surface measures capacitance changes caused by nearby hands, producing a proximity image that is interpreted as touch shapes.
works.technique_zh: 表面下方的发射和接收电极网格测量手靠近时引起的电容变化，形成一张“接近度图像”，再解释为触摸形状。
works.exercise_en: Use a webcam under a glass table or a phone multi-touch page to build a 'dough' simulation that you can squeeze with two hands. Twist: make the dough remember where it was touched most and glow there.
works.exercise_zh: 用玻璃桌下方的摄像头或手机多点触控网页，做一个可以用双手揉捏的“面团”模拟；变体：让面团记住被触摸最多的地方并在那里发光。

video.video_title: SmartSkin: An Infrastructure for Freehand Manipulations on Interactive Surfaces (CHI2002)

works.title: Tinmith Glove User Interface
works.description: Menus are mapped onto the fingers of pinch gloves: the user presses thumb to finger to pick commands while walking outdoors in AR, and points with tracked thumbs to place objects.
works.description_zh: 菜单被映射到捏合手套的各个手指上：用户在户外 AR 中边走边用拇指碰手指选命令，并用被追踪的拇指指点来放置物体。
works.idea_en: Your fingers become the menu when there is no mouse outdoors.
works.idea_zh: 户外没有鼠标时，你的手指就是菜单。
works.technique: Uses conductive pinch gloves for discrete menu selection and fiducial markers on the thumbs for 3D cursor tracking by the head-mounted camera.
works.technique_zh: 用导电捏合手套进行离散的菜单选择，并借助拇指上的标记让头戴摄像头追踪三维光标。
works.exercise_en: Write four commands on your fingertips, and build a phone app where a partner triggers the matching AR action when you tap thumb to finger. Twist: design a two-level menu using both hands.
works.exercise_zh: 在指尖上写下四个命令，做一个手机应用，你用拇指碰某根手指时，同伴触发对应的 AR 动作；变体：用双手设计一个两级菜单。

video.video_title: Tinmith Outdoor Augmented Reality Modelling 2002 - tinmith-glove-user-interface-oct2002.mpg

works.title: Trash Mirror
works.description: Irregular pieces of trash collected from the streets become motorised pixels that tilt to reflect the viewer's image.
works.idea_zh: 用街头垃圾碎片做成会映照你的镜子
works.technique: Each irregular trash piece sits on a motor mapped to a region of the camera image, rotating to present a lighter or darker face.
works.exercise_zh: 收集教室里的废纸片做成不规则“像素”，用几个舵机+摄像头做一个小型原型；变化：每块碎片对应它在画面中的真实形状区域。

video.video_title: "Trash Mirror" (2002) by Daniel Rozin

works.description_zh: 从街头收集来的不规则垃圾碎片变成了电动像素，它们倾斜转动，映出观众的影像。
works.idea_en: Make a mirror that reflects you out of scraps of street trash.
works.technique_zh: 每块不规则的垃圾碎片都装在一个电机上，对应摄像头画面中的一个区域，通过旋转呈现较亮或较暗的一面。
works.exercise_en: Collect scrap paper from the classroom to make irregular 'pixels', and build a small prototype with a few servos and a camera. Twist: map each scrap to a region matching its real shape in the image.

works.title: Vivisector (with Chris Haring)
works.description: Four dancers are sculpted solely by projected light — no stage lighting — so their bodies appear sliced, dissolved and multiplied by the projection.
works.idea_zh: 只用投影光照亮舞者，让身体被光切片、溶解
works.technique: Projectors act as the only light source ('dancing light'), with video masks choreographed to reveal and fragment specific body regions.
works.exercise_zh: 关掉教室灯，只用投影仪的黑白遮罩照亮同学的局部身体；变化：用摄像头追踪手的位置让光斑自动跟随。

video.video_title: Vivisector, Part 4 – Klaus Obermaier, Chris Haring

works.description_zh: 四位舞者完全由投影光来塑造，没有任何舞台灯光，他们的身体在投影下仿佛被切片、溶解和复制。
works.idea_en: Light the dancers only with projection so their bodies get sliced and dissolved by light.
works.technique_zh: 投影仪是唯一的光源（“舞动的光”），经过编排的视频遮罩显现并切分身体的特定部位。
works.exercise_en: Turn off the classroom lights and use only black-and-white projector masks to light parts of a classmate's body. Twist: track the hand with a camera so the spot of light follows it automatically.

works.title: Body Movies (Relational Architecture 6)
works.description: Thousands of street portraits are projected onto a building façade but only become visible inside the giant shadows of passers-by, whose silhouettes grow from 2 to 25 metres depending on their distance from floor lights.
works.idea_zh: 你的巨大影子才是看见陌生人肖像的“窗口”
works.technique: Robotic projectors show portraits on a façade washed out by bright floor lamps; a camera tracks shadow regions, and when a shadow matches a portrait the scene advances.
works.exercise_zh: 一台投影仪投图片、另一盏强光灯把画面“冲白”，同学的影子里才能看见图片；变化：用摄像头检测影子是否完全盖住某张脸来触发下一张。

video.video_title: Body Movies

works.description_zh: 数千幅街头肖像被投射到建筑立面上，但只有在路人巨大的影子里才能看见；根据人与地面灯的距离，影子的高度从 2 米到 25 米不等。
works.idea_en: Your giant shadow is the only window through which strangers' portraits can be seen.
works.technique_zh: 机械投影仪把肖像投到被明亮地灯冲淡的立面上；摄像头追踪影子区域，当影子与某幅肖像重合时，场景便切换到下一幕。
works.exercise_en: Have one projector show images while a strong lamp washes the picture out, so the images are visible only inside classmates' shadows. Twist: use a camera to check whether a shadow fully covers a face, and trigger the next image when it does.

works.title: Tijuana Projection
works.description: Women who work in Tijuana's maquiladora factories wear a head-mounted camera and microphone, and their faces and testimonies are projected live onto the huge sphere of the city's Omnimax theater.
works.description_zh: 在蒂华纳加工厂工作的女性戴上头戴摄像头和麦克风，她们的脸和讲述被实时投到城市球幕影院巨大的球面外墙上。
works.idea_en: A wearable camera turns a monument-sized building into the live face of one person.
works.idea_zh: 一个可穿戴摄像头，就能把纪念碑般的建筑变成一个人的实时面孔。
works.technique: A lightweight headset with a camera fixed on the wearer's face streams video and audio to projectors aimed at the 60-foot dome, mixed with prerecorded segments.
works.technique_zh: 固定对准佩戴者面部的轻型头戴摄像头把视频和音频传给对准 18 米球面的投影机，并与预录片段交替播放。
works.exercise_en: Mount a phone on a selfie-stick headband pointing at your face, stream it to a projector and project your talking face onto a round object (a balloon or dome) in class. Twist: let a classmate interview you live while the audience only sees the projected face.
works.exercise_zh: 把手机用自拍杆头带固定、镜头对准自己的脸，实时推流到投影仪，把说话的脸投到教室里一个圆形物体（气球或穹顶）上；变体：让同学现场采访你，观众只能看到投影出来的脸。

video.video_title: CLOSEUP Krzysztof Wodiczko, "Tijuana Projection", inSITE2000.

works.title: Tinmith-Metro Outdoor AR Modelling
works.description: Standing outside a building, the user wears pinch gloves and 'captures' its walls by pointing and pinching, building a 3D model of the real building on the spot.
works.description_zh: 站在建筑外，用户戴着捏合手套，通过指点和捏合“捕捉”墙面，现场建出真实建筑的三维模型。
works.idea_en: Model architecture by standing in front of it and grabbing its shape with your hands.
works.idea_zh: 站在建筑面前，用双手“抓取”它的形状来建模。
works.technique: Uses working-planes projected from the tracked head and gloves to intersect infinite planes into solid building geometry, all on a wearable backpack computer.
works.technique_zh: 在可穿戴背包电脑上，由追踪的头部和手套投射出工作平面，让无限平面相交生成实体建筑几何体。
works.exercise_en: Use a phone AR measuring or plane-detection app to trace the walls of a room and export a floor plan, then compare with a tape-measure drawing. Twist: model a building outside using only photos taken from the pavement.
works.exercise_zh: 用手机 AR 测量或平面检测 App 描出房间的墙面并导出平面图，再与卷尺手绘的图对比；变体：只用在人行道上拍的照片为室外建筑建模。

video.video_title: Tinmith Outdoor Augmented Reality Modelling 2001 - building-capture.avi

works.title: ARQuake
works.description: A player with a backpack computer, head-mounted display and toy gun walks across the university campus shooting Quake monsters that appear among the real buildings.
works.description_zh: 玩家背着背包电脑、戴着头显、手持玩具枪，在大学校园里行走，射击出现在真实建筑之间的 Quake 怪物。
works.idea_en: Turn a real campus into a first-person shooter level.
works.idea_zh: 把真实的校园变成第一人称射击游戏的关卡。
works.technique: Modifies the Quake engine to render only monsters and items in see-through view, driven by GPS, a head tracker and a campus model for occlusion.
works.technique_zh: 修改 Quake 引擎，在透视视图中只渲染怪物和道具，由 GPS、头部追踪器以及用于遮挡的校园模型驱动。
works.exercise_en: Design a location-based phone AR game where virtual creatures spawn at three GPS points on campus and players must reach them to catch them. Twist: let creatures hide behind real walls using a simple occlusion box.
works.exercise_zh: 设计一款基于位置的手机 AR 游戏，虚拟生物在校园三个 GPS 点出现，玩家必须跑到那里去捉；变体：用一个简单的遮挡盒让生物躲在真实墙后。

video.video_title: ARQuake 2006 - quake1.dv

works.title: Augmented Surfaces
works.description: Laptops placed on a projected table and wall become part of one continuous workspace: you drag a document off the laptop screen onto the table, and physical objects with tags get digital data attached to them.
works.description_zh: 把笔记本电脑放在投影桌面上，笔记本、桌面和墙面就连成一个连续的工作空间：文档可以从笔记本屏幕直接拖到桌面上，贴了标签的实物也能被“挂”上数字数据。
works.idea_en: The whole room becomes one desktop: data flows off screens onto tables, walls and objects.
works.idea_zh: 整间屋子变成一个大桌面：数据可以从屏幕流到桌子、墙面和实物上。
works.technique: Ceiling cameras recognize laptops and tagged objects and track their positions, while projectors draw the shared workspace; a 'hyperdragging' cursor crosses from the laptop into the projection.
works.technique_zh: 天花板上的摄像头识别并追踪笔记本和带标签的物体，投影仪绘制共享工作区；“超级拖拽”光标可以从笔记本屏幕一路移到投影区域。
works.exercise_en: Point a projector and webcam at a desk and let students drag a picture from a laptop browser onto the projected table, where it sticks to a paper marker. Twist: when two markers touch, merge their pictures.
works.exercise_zh: 把投影仪和摄像头对准一张桌子，让学生把浏览器里的图片从笔记本“拖”到投影桌面上，并粘在一张纸质标记上；变体：两个标记碰到一起时，把它们的图片合成一张。

video.video_title: Augmented Surfaces (CHI'99)

works.title: Text Rain (with Romy Achituv)
works.description: Participants see a mirrored video of themselves while coloured letters from a poem fall like rain; the letters land on and rest on anything dark, so people catch, lift and spill lines of text with their bodies.
works.idea_zh: 用身体接住从天而降的诗句字母
works.technique: Each falling letter checks the brightness of the live camera pixel below it and stops falling when the pixel is darker than a threshold, so the body's silhouette becomes a physical surface.
works.exercise_zh: 用p5.js摄像头做“字母雨”：每个字母遇到暗像素就停住；变化：换成自己写的一首诗，并让被接住的字母连成可读的词时发出声音。

video.video_title: Camille Utterback - Text Rain

works.description_zh: 参与者看到自己的镜像视频，同时一首诗的彩色字母像雨一样落下；字母会停落在任何深色的东西上，于是人们可以用身体接住、托起并洒落一行行文字。
works.idea_en: Catch the letters of a poem falling from the sky with your body.
works.technique_zh: 每个下落的字母都会检查其下方实时摄像头像素的亮度，当像素比阈值更暗时就停止下落，于是身体的剪影就成了一个实体表面。
works.exercise_en: Make 'letter rain' with a p5.js camera sketch, where each letter stops when it meets a dark pixel. Twist: use a poem you wrote yourself, and play a sound when caught letters line up into a readable word.

works.title: Wooden Mirror
works.description: 830 small wooden tiles tilt with individual motors so the light they catch forms a live, wooden reflection of whoever stands in front.
works.idea_zh: 用会转动的木片拼出你的实时镜像
works.technique: A hidden camera image is downsampled to the tile grid and each pixel's brightness sets a servo angle that changes how much light the wooden tile reflects.
works.exercise_zh: 用8×8舵机+卡纸片做一面“机械镜子”，由摄像头低分辨率图像控制角度；变化：换成自己选的材料（纽扣、瓶盖），比较不同材料的“像素感”。

video.video_title: "Wooden Mirror" (1999) by Daniel Rozin

works.description_zh: 830 块小木片由各自的电机控制倾斜，它们捕捉到的光形成了站在面前之人的实时木质倒影。
works.idea_en: Piece together your live mirror image from turning wooden tiles.
works.technique_zh: 隐藏摄像头的画面被降采样到木片网格的分辨率，每个像素的亮度决定一个舵机的角度，从而改变木片反射的光量。
works.exercise_en: Build a 'mechanical mirror' from an 8x8 grid of servos and card tiles, with angles controlled by a low-resolution camera image. Twist: switch to a material of your choice (buttons, bottle caps) and compare how 'pixel-like' different materials feel.

works.title: Boundary Functions
works.description: An overhead projector draws lines on the floor between everyone standing in the room, dividing it into personal Voronoi cells that grow, shrink and snap as people move.
works.idea_zh: 把看不见的“个人空间”用地面上的沃罗诺伊线画出来，人越多空间越小
works.technique: An overhead camera tracks each person's floor position and a Voronoi diagram of those points is computed in real time and projected back onto the floor from above.
works.exercise_zh: 用俯拍摄像头+投影仪（或手机俯拍+p5.js）追踪同学站位，实时计算并投影沃罗诺伊分界线；加一个变化：让每个格子的颜色随其面积变化，面积越小越红。

video.video_title: Boundary Functions - Interactive Art by Scott Snibbe (1998) HD Version

works.description_zh: 一台俯投的投影仪在房间里每个站着的人之间画出线条，把地面划分成个人的沃罗诺伊（Voronoi）单元，随着人们移动，这些单元会扩大、缩小、骤然改变。
works.idea_en: Draw invisible 'personal space' on the floor as Voronoi lines, so the more people there are, the less space each gets.
works.technique_zh: 俯拍摄像头追踪每个人在地面上的位置，实时计算这些点的沃罗诺伊图，并从上方投射回地面。
works.exercise_en: Use an overhead camera and projector (or a phone filming from above with p5.js) to track where classmates stand, and compute and project Voronoi boundaries in real time. Twist: color each cell by its area, turning redder as it shrinks.

works.title: D.A.V.E. – digital amplified video engine (with Chris Haring)
works.description: A solo dancer's body becomes the projection screen: morphing faces, ageing and impossible body distortions are mapped precisely onto the moving performer.
works.idea_zh: 把舞者身体本身当成屏幕，投射出不可能的变形
works.technique: Pre-rendered video is choreographed frame-by-frame with the dancer so the projection lands on the body, relying on rehearsed timing rather than tracking.
works.exercise_zh: 让一位同学穿白衣站在投影前，按排练好的节奏把预先剪好的脸部/纹理视频投到身上；变化：加一个用摄像头实时跟随的小光斑。

video.video_title: Klaus Obermaier, Chris Haring: D.A.V.E. – digital amplified video engine - 1998/2000

works.description_zh: 独舞者的身体本身成了投影屏幕：变形的面孔、衰老过程和不可能的身体扭曲被精确地映射到运动中的表演者身上。
works.idea_en: Use the dancer's own body as the screen and project impossible transformations onto it.
works.technique_zh: 预渲染的视频与舞者逐帧编排，使投影落在身体上；依靠的是排练好的时机，而不是追踪。
works.exercise_en: Have a classmate in white clothes stand in front of the projector, and project pre-cut face or texture videos onto them following a rehearsed rhythm. Twist: add a small spot of light that follows them live via a camera.

works.title: Pick-and-Drop
works.description: A user taps a file on one computer with a pen, physically carries the pen to another screen and taps again to drop it there, as if data were an object you can pick up.
works.description_zh: 用户用笔在一台电脑上点一下某个文件，拿着笔走到另一块屏幕前再点一下，文件就被“放”了过去，好像数据是可以拿起来的实物。
works.idea_en: Treat digital data like a physical thing you can pick up with one device and drop into another.
works.idea_zh: 把数字数据当成实物：在一个设备上拿起，到另一个设备上放下。
works.technique: Each pen has a unique ID; tapping registers the pen ID and the selected object with a network server, and tapping another screen with the same pen retrieves it.
works.technique_zh: 每支笔有唯一 ID；点选时服务器记录“这支笔拿着哪个对象”，用同一支笔点另一块屏幕时再把对象取出来。
works.exercise_en: Make two phones and a laptop share a 'grab' gesture: pinch on one screen to pick an image, then tap another device within five seconds to drop it there. Twist: let the image 'spill' if you walk too slowly.
works.exercise_zh: 让两部手机和一台笔记本共享一个“抓取”手势：在一块屏上捏合拿起一张图片，五秒内点另一台设备即可放下；变体：如果走得太慢，图片就会“洒出来”。

video.video_title: Pick-and-Drop (UIST'97, CHI'98)

works.title: 3D CyberCode
works.description: Printed 2D barcode cards are placed in front of a camera and each one sprouts a 3D object that stays registered to the card as it is tilted and moved, years before ARToolKit.
works.description_zh: 把印有二维条码的卡片放到摄像头前，每张卡片上都会“长出”一个 3D 物体，卡片倾斜移动时物体也紧紧贴合，这比 ARToolKit 还早好几年。
works.idea_en: A printed code can be both an ID and a 3D anchor for virtual objects.
works.idea_zh: 一张印刷的码既是身份标识，也是虚拟物体的三维锚点。
works.technique: The system decodes a square 2D matrix code and estimates its 3D pose from the code's corner points, then renders a model on top of the camera image.
works.technique_zh: 系统解码方形二维矩阵码，并根据码的四个角点估算其三维姿态，再把模型渲染到摄像头画面上。
works.exercise_en: Make a deck of six marker cards with an AR library (for example AR.js or MindAR) and give each card a 3D creature; when two cards touch, spawn a third creature between them. Twist: let players trade cards so the creatures 'travel' between tables.
works.exercise_zh: 用 AR 库（如 AR.js 或 MindAR）做一副六张的标记卡牌，每张卡对应一只 3D 小生物；两张卡靠在一起时，在中间生成第三只；变体：让同学交换卡牌，小生物就在不同桌子之间“旅行”。

video.video_title: 3D CyberCode 1996 (the origin of PS3 Eye of Judgment)

works.title: TransVision
works.description: Several people around a table each hold a small palmtop display and see the same virtual 3D model sitting on the real table, so they can discuss and point at it together.
works.description_zh: 几个人围坐在桌边，各自拿着一块掌上屏幕，都能看到桌上“放着”同一个虚拟 3D 模型，于是可以一起讨论、一起指点。
works.idea_en: Shared handheld AR: many small windows onto one virtual object in the middle of a real table.
works.idea_zh: 共享手持 AR：多扇小窗口同时看向真实桌面中央的同一个虚拟物体。
works.technique: Each palmtop is a video see-through display whose position is tracked (likely by magnetic sensors), and a shared scene graph keeps the model in the same place for every viewer.
works.technique_zh: 每块掌上屏都是视频透视显示器，其位置被追踪（很可能使用电磁传感器），共享场景图保证每个观看者看到的模型位置一致。
works.exercise_en: Build a two-phone shared AR scene (for example with an image target or a shared anchor) where both players see the same virtual building on a desk and can move one block each. Twist: give each phone a different 'lens' that shows a different layer of the same object.
works.exercise_zh: 做一个两部手机共享的 AR 场景（可用图像目标或共享锚点），两人都能在桌上看到同一栋虚拟建筑，并各自移动一块积木；变体：给每部手机一个不同的“镜头”，分别看到同一物体的不同层次。

video.video_title: TransVision: Shared Hand-held Augmented Reality (1996)

works.title: NaviCam
works.description: A palmtop screen with a small camera is held up to the world; when it sees color-coded ID tags on shelves or doors it overlays context information on the live video, like a magnifying glass for hidden data.
works.description_zh: 把带小摄像头的掌上屏幕举向周围环境，一旦看到书架或门上的彩色 ID 标签，就在实时画面上叠加相关信息，像一把能看见隐藏数据的放大镜。
works.idea_en: Hold a screen up to the world and it reveals the information attached to things.
works.idea_zh: 把屏幕举向世界，它就显示出物体身上“附着”的信息。
works.technique: A camera tethered to a workstation recognizes printed color-code tags in the video stream and draws text labels next to them on a handheld LCD (video see-through).
works.technique_zh: 摄像头画面传给工作站识别打印的彩色编码标签，再把文字标签绘制在手持液晶屏的实时视频上（视频透视式 AR）。
works.exercise_en: Print five ArUco markers, stick them on classroom objects and build a phone web page that shows a different 'secret note' next to each marker when the camera sees it. Twist: make the note change depending on how close the phone is to the marker.
works.exercise_zh: 打印五个 ArUco 标记贴在教室物品上，做一个手机网页：摄像头看到哪个标记，就在旁边显示一条对应的“秘密便签”；变体：让便签内容随手机与标记的距离远近而变化。

video.video_title: NaviCam hand held AR system (1994-1995)

works.title: Hirshhorn Museum, Washington, D.C.
works.description: Giant images of hands holding a gun, candles and a bundle of microphones are projected around the drum-shaped Hirshhorn Museum, turning the building into a political body on the National Mall.
works.description_zh: 巨大的手握手枪、蜡烛和一束麦克风的影像被投在圆筒形的赫希洪博物馆外墙上，让这座建筑在国家广场上变成一具发表政治宣言的身体。
works.idea_en: Project a body onto a building so the architecture speaks about the power around it.
works.idea_zh: 把身体投到建筑上，让建筑对周围的权力发声。
works.technique: Large-format slide projectors throw still images onto the curved façade, with the images composed to wrap around the building's cylinder.
works.technique_zh: 大画幅幻灯投影机把静态图像投到弧形立面上，画面经过专门构图，能环绕整个圆柱形建筑。
works.exercise_en: Pick a campus building, photograph its façade, and design three still projection images (drawn over the photo) that make the building 'say' something about what happens inside. Twist: only use hands.
works.exercise_zh: 选一栋校园建筑，拍下立面照片，在照片上设计三张投影图像，让建筑“说出”里面正在发生的事情；变体：画面里只能出现手。

video.video_title: Krzysztof Wodiczko on his 1988 Hirshhorn Museum projection

works.title: CRITTER (VIDEOPLACE)
works.description: A small graphic creature chases a visitor's silhouette, climbs up their arm, dangles from a fingertip and does a little dance when it reaches the top of the head.
works.description_zh: 一只小小的图形生物追着观众的剪影跑，顺着手臂往上爬，吊在指尖上晃，爬到头顶时还会跳一段小舞。
works.idea_en: A virtual pet that understands the shape of your body.
works.idea_zh: 一只能“读懂”你身体形状的虚拟宠物。
works.technique: The creature's behavior rules react to the tracked silhouette's outline, finding hands and head from extremities of the contour.
works.technique_zh: 小生物的行为规则会对追踪到的剪影轮廓做出反应，通过轮廓的端点判断手和头的位置。
works.exercise_en: Build a creature in a webcam sketch that walks along the edge of your body mask, jumps to your highest point and falls if you move too fast. Twist: give it moods so it avoids people who wave aggressively.
works.exercise_zh: 在网络摄像头草图里做一只沿着人体轮廓边缘行走的小生物，它会跳到你身体的最高点，动作太快它就会掉下来；变体：给它加上情绪，遇到挥手太猛的人就躲开。

video.video_title: Myron Krueger's Critter

works.title: VIDEOPLACE
works.description: A visitor's live silhouette appears on a large screen and can draw with a finger, juggle graphic objects, or touch the silhouette of another person in a different room.
works.description_zh: 观众的实时剪影出现在大屏幕上，可以用手指画线、抛接图形物体，甚至去“触碰”另一个房间里另一个人的剪影。
works.idea_en: Your camera silhouette is your body in the computer world, no gear required.
works.idea_zh: 摄像头里的剪影就是你在计算机世界里的身体，不需要任何穿戴设备。
works.technique: A camera against a backlit wall extracts the body outline in real time with custom hardware, and programs test the outline for contact with graphic objects (the video shows the 1985 version).
works.technique_zh: 摄像头对着背光墙面，用定制硬件实时提取人体轮廓，程序再判断轮廓是否碰到了图形物体（视频为 1985 年版本）。
works.exercise_en: Use a webcam and body segmentation in p5.js to make five mini VIDEOPLACE scenes: draw with a fingertip, bounce a ball off your arm, hold a creature in your palm. Twist: connect two laptops so two remote silhouettes can 'shake hands'.
works.exercise_zh: 用网络摄像头和 p5.js 人体分割做五个迷你 VIDEOPLACE 场景：用指尖画画、用手臂弹球、让小生物站在手心；变体：连接两台笔记本，让两个异地的剪影“握手”。

video.video_title: Videoplace (1985)

keys._note: Curated Key Creators and their guided tours. Order of groups, creators and highlights is the tour order. Edit freely; rebuild with python3 tools/build_data.py.

groups.desc_zh: 网络里被引用最多的一群人。很多后来的创作者，都是顺着他们找到的。
groups.desc_en: The most-cited people in the network. Many later creators were found by following their trail.

groups.desc_zh: 许多 AR 交互点子的“第一次”，出自这些实验室的论文和 demo 视频。
groups.desc_en: Many AR interaction ideas first appeared in these labs' papers and demo videos.

groups.desc_zh: 每当出现新设备、新 API，他们就公开做出一个小实验。最适合“每周一个原型”式的教学。
groups.desc_en: Whenever a new device or API appears, they publish a small experiment. Ideal for a prototype-a-week style of teaching.

groups.desc_zh: 回答“为什么要做 AR”：把技术变成观点、表演和公共空间里的体验。
groups.desc_en: Answers to “why make AR at all”: technology turned into a point of view, a performance, or an experience in public space.

creators.tagline_zh: 把声音、文字和身体放进空间：诗意 AR 的原点。
creators.intro_zh: Zach Lieberman 是 openFrameworks 和 School for Poetic Computation 的联合创始人。二十年来他反复做同一件事：让看不见的东西（声音、笔迹、动作）在空间里留下形状。他的 AR 作品技术上往往很简单，靠的是一个清楚、好玩、能立刻被理解的点子。
creators.learn_zh: 学他怎么把一个技术能力（追踪、录音、画线）变成一个一句话就能讲清楚的诗意点子。

highlights.note_zh: 2005 年的起点：手绘的墨迹被摄像头识别后活了过来。先看这件，理解他“纸与屏幕之间”的思路。
highlights.note_en: The 2005 starting point: hand-drawn ink comes alive once the camera sees it. Watch this first to understand his idea of working between paper and screen.

highlights.note_zh: 用眼动追踪让瘫痪的涂鸦艺术家重新作画，也是开源协作的典范。技术为一个具体的人服务。
highlights.note_en: Eye tracking lets a paralyzed graffiti artist draw again; also a model of open-source collaboration. Technology in service of one specific person.

highlights.note_zh: 本项目的种子作品：每个声音都留在它发出的位置，走回去就能倒放。ARKit 刚出现时最有诗意的一个回应。
highlights.note_en: The seed of this project: every sound stays where it was made, and walking back through it plays it in reverse. The most poetic response to ARKit's arrival.

highlights.note_zh: 和 Molmol Kuo 做成了人人可用的 App：在空中写字、让文字跟着运动。从个人实验到大众工具的一步。
highlights.note_en: With Molmol Kuo, turned into an app anyone can use: write in the air and let text follow motion. The step from personal experiment to public tool.

highlights.note_zh: 在 Snap Spectacles 眼镜里，与 Shantell Martin 合作的一首可以走进去读的诗。阅读顺序由你的脚步决定。
highlights.note_en: On Snap Spectacles, with Shantell Martin: a poem you read by walking through it. Your footsteps set the reading order.

creators.tagline_en: Sound, text and the body placed in space: the origin of poetic AR.
creators.intro_en: Zach Lieberman co-founded openFrameworks and the School for Poetic Computation. For twenty years he has done one thing again and again: give invisible things — sound, handwriting, motion — a shape in space. His AR pieces are often technically simple; their strength is an idea that is clear, playful and instantly understood.
creators.learn_en: How to turn a technical capability (tracking, recording, drawing a line) into a poetic idea you can explain in one sentence.

creators.tagline_zh: 互动艺术教育的源头：让声音、影子和手变成可以看见的形状。
creators.intro_zh: Golan Levin 是卡内基梅隆大学 STUDIO for Creative Inquiry 的负责人，也是很多创意编程者的老师。他的作品常常把人的声音或身体“放大”成视觉，并且总在追问：机器是怎么看人的？
creators.learn_zh: 学“增强”的另一种含义：不一定叠加虚拟物体，也可以是把人本来就有的东西（声音、手势、影子）变得可见。

highlights.note_zh: 说话和唱歌的声音变成从嘴里冒出来的图形。投影 AR 的经典之作，和 Zach Lieberman 等人合作完成。
highlights.note_en: Speech and song become shapes that pour out of the mouth. A classic of projection AR, made with Zach Lieberman and others.

highlights.note_zh: 跺脚产生的声音变成从天而降的虚拟物体，落在你的影子上。声音、身体、投影三者合一。
highlights.note_en: Stomping makes virtual objects rain down onto your shadow. Sound, body and projection in one piece.

highlights.note_zh: 把你的手实时变形：多一根手指，或者手指会自己弯曲。最小的“增强”带来最强烈的身体感。
highlights.note_en: Your hand, transformed live: an extra finger, fingers that bend on their own. The smallest augmentation, the strongest bodily effect.

highlights.note_zh: 用 ARKit 重做 1994 年 Jeffrey Shaw 的经典作品《Golden Calf》。适合讨论 AR 的历史谱系。
highlights.note_en: Jeffrey Shaw's 1994 Golden Calf, re-made with ARKit. Good for discussing AR's lineage.

creators.tagline_en: A source of interactive-art education: making voice, shadow and hands visible as form.
creators.intro_en: Golan Levin directs the STUDIO for Creative Inquiry at Carnegie Mellon and has taught many creative coders. His works often amplify a person's voice or body into visuals, and keep asking: how does a machine see a person?
creators.learn_en: Another meaning of “augment”: not adding virtual objects, but making what people already have — voice, gesture, shadow — visible.

creators.tagline_zh: 在整个网络里被关联最多的人：让人脸追踪和机器视觉成为艺术材料。
creators.intro_zh: Kyle McDonald 写了早期最流行的开源人脸追踪工具（ofxFaceTracker），很多人脸 AR 作品都建立在他的代码之上。他的作品不断测试“在摄像头面前，身份和隐私意味着什么”。
creators.learn_zh: 学怎么把一项底层能力（人脸追踪）开源出去，然后用它做出引人思考、甚至有点不安的作品。

highlights.note_zh: 2011 年的实时换脸，比 Snapchat 早了好几年。看这件就能理解后来所有面部滤镜的源头。
highlights.note_en: Real-time face swap in 2011, years before Snapchat. The root of every face filter that followed.

highlights.note_zh: 两座城市的人通过镜子“交换”相似的脸：一面把陌生人连接起来的 AR 镜子。
highlights.note_en: People in two cities “swap” similar faces through a mirror: an AR mirror that connects strangers.

highlights.note_zh: 用几十个迪斯科镜面球，加上经过计算机视觉标定的投影仪，把整个房间点满移动的光斑。与 Jonas Jongejan 合作。
highlights.note_en: Dozens of mirror balls and computer-vision-calibrated projectors fill a room with moving points of light. With Jonas Jongejan.

highlights.note_zh: 一场“穿越真实空间的虚拟蹦极”：观众被吊着戴上头显，看到的是一台沿钢丝坠落的摄像头的实时画面。身体感受和视角被分离。
highlights.note_en: A “virtual bungee jump through a real space”: visitors in a harness see the live feed of a camera dropping along a wire. Body sensation and viewpoint are split apart.

creators.tagline_en: The most-connected person in the network: face tracking and machine vision as artistic material.
creators.intro_en: Kyle McDonald wrote ofxFaceTracker, the most popular early open-source face tracker, and many face-AR works are built on his code. His pieces keep testing what identity and privacy mean in front of a camera.
creators.learn_en: How to open-source a low-level capability (face tracking) and then use it to make work that is thought-provoking, even unsettling.

creators.name: Design I/O — Theo Watson & Emily Gobeille
creators.tagline_zh: 儿童互动投影的标杆：全身交互，最适合教学复刻。
creators.intro_zh: Theo Watson（openFrameworks 联合创始人）和 Emily Gobeille 组成的 Design I/O，十多年来为博物馆做大型互动空间。孩子用身体、沙子和纸就能和整个房间的虚拟生态互动。
creators.learn_zh: 学怎么为“不会看说明书的人”设计：没有界面、没有按钮，身体一动就有反馈。

highlights.note_zh: 用激光笔在大楼墙面上涂鸦（与 Graffiti Research Lab 合作）。建筑尺度的投影 AR，代码开源。
highlights.note_en: Graffiti on a building with a laser pointer (with Graffiti Research Lab). Architecture-scale projection AR, open-sourced.

highlights.note_zh: 孩子用身体在地上“种”出树，引水浇灌森林。Design I/O 风格的起点。
highlights.note_en: Children grow trees with their bodies and steer water to the forest. Where the Design I/O style began.

highlights.note_zh: 举起手臂就能操纵巨大的投影木偶。最直观的全身交互之一。
highlights.note_en: Raise your arms to puppeteer giant projected creatures. One of the most direct full-body interactions.

highlights.note_zh: 纽约科学馆的大型生态系统：六个环境通过水流连在一起，孩子们一起决定生态的走向。多人协作的范例。
highlights.note_en: A large ecosystem at the New York Hall of Science: six habitats linked by water, where children decide together how the ecosystem evolves. A model of multiplayer collaboration.

highlights.note_zh: 翻开真实的书，页面上的动物就活了。纸质书与投影的结合，很适合改造成课堂作业。
highlights.note_en: Turn a real page and the animals on it come alive. Paper plus projection; easy to adapt into a class assignment.

creators.tagline_en: The benchmark for children's interactive projection: full-body interaction, ideal for classroom re-creation.
creators.intro_en: Design I/O — Theo Watson (co-founder of openFrameworks) and Emily Gobeille — has built large interactive spaces for museums for more than a decade. Children use their bodies, sand and paper to interact with a room-sized virtual ecosystem.
creators.learn_en: How to design for people who will never read instructions: no interface, no buttons, instant feedback to the body.

creators.tagline_zh: 把整个房间变成屏幕：投影式空间 AR 的研究源头。
creators.intro_zh: Hrvoje Benko 和 Andy Wilson 在微软研究院做了十多年“不用戴眼镜的 AR”：用投影仪加深度相机，让墙、桌子、家具都变成可交互的表面。许多后来的 MR 游戏点子，最早都出现在他们的 demo 里。
creators.learn_zh: 学空间 AR（Spatial AR）的思路：先理解房间的几何，再决定内容在哪里出现、怎么与现实对齐。

highlights.note_zh: 2010 年：用多台投影仪加深度相机，把任何表面变成触摸屏，还能把内容“拿”在手上带走。
highlights.note_en: 2010: several projectors and depth cameras turn any surface into a touchscreen, and you can carry content in your hand.

highlights.note_zh: 游戏画面溢出电视，延伸到整面墙上。用最少的硬件，最大化地扩展视野。
highlights.note_en: The game spills out of the TV onto the whole wall. Minimal hardware, maximum field of view.

highlights.note_zh: 整个客厅变成游戏场，怪物从墙上爬出来。今天 Quest 混合现实游戏的前身。
highlights.note_en: The living room becomes a game, with monsters climbing out of the walls. A forerunner of today's Quest mixed-reality games.

highlights.note_zh: 两个人面对面对战，各自看到正确的透视。不戴头显的多人 AR。
highlights.note_en: Two people face off and each sees correct perspective. Multiplayer AR without headsets.

highlights.note_zh: 把远方的人三维捕捉后，以真人大小投影进你的房间，坐在你真实的沙发上。远程临场的早期形态。
highlights.note_en: A remote person is captured in 3D and projected life-size into your room, sitting on your real couch. An early form of telepresence.

creators.tagline_en: Turning a whole room into a display: the research source of projected spatial AR.
creators.intro_en: Hrvoje Benko and Andy Wilson spent over a decade at Microsoft Research on “AR without glasses”: projectors plus depth cameras that make walls, tables and furniture interactive. Many later mixed-reality game ideas first appeared in their demos.
creators.learn_en: The spatial-AR mindset: understand the room's geometry first, then decide where content appears and how it aligns with reality.

creators.tagline_zh: 让数字信息长出实体：可变形界面的源头。
creators.intro_zh: 石井裕（Hiroshi Ishii）领导的 MIT Tangible Media Group 提出了“Tangible Bits”和“Radical Atoms”：数字信息不应只困在玻璃屏幕里，而应该能被触摸、被推动。他们的针阵显示器系列至今仍是最震撼的 demo 之一。
creators.learn_zh: 学“反向 AR”：不是把虚拟叠加到现实上，而是让现实的物理形态随数字信息而改变。

highlights.note_zh: 虚拟图形和实体针阵无缝融合：同一个形状，一半是真的、一半是投影出来的。
highlights.note_en: Virtual graphics and a physical pin array merge: the same shape is half real, half projected.

highlights.note_zh: 最著名的一件：900 根可动的针实时变成物体的形状，还能远程“握手”。看完会重新理解什么是界面。
highlights.note_en: The most famous one: 900 moving pins take the shape of objects in real time, and even shake hands remotely. It changes what you think an interface is.

highlights.note_zh: 远方的人通过针阵，推动你桌上的真实物体。远程临场从“看见”变成“碰到”。
highlights.note_en: A remote person pushes real objects on your table through the pin display. Telepresence moves from seeing to touching.

highlights.note_zh: 针阵变成家具和艺术装置，在米兰设计周展出。研究原型走向设计语言。
highlights.note_en: Pin displays become furniture and art at Milan Design Week. A research prototype turned into design language.

creators.tagline_en: Giving digital information a physical body: the origin of shape-changing interfaces.
creators.intro_en: Hiroshi Ishii's MIT Tangible Media Group proposed “Tangible Bits” and “Radical Atoms”: digital information should not be trapped behind glass but be touchable and movable. Their pin-display series remains among the most striking demos.
creators.learn_en: “Reverse AR”: instead of overlaying the virtual on the real, reality's physical shape changes with digital information.

creators.tagline_zh: 把手指和墙面变成界面：可穿戴 AR 的第一次大众展示。
creators.intro_zh: Pattie Maes 领导的 MIT Fluid Interfaces 组，2009 年由 Pranav Mistry 展示了 SixthSense：脖子上挂一个投影仪和摄像头，就能在手掌、报纸、墙面上操作信息。那场 TED 演讲让全世界第一次想象“随身 AR”。
creators.learn_zh: 学用最便宜的硬件（投影仪、摄像头、彩色指套）去演示一个大想法，并用讲故事的方式让人看懂。

highlights.note_zh: 在手掌上拨号，在报纸上播放视频，用手指比一个框就能拍照。可穿戴投影 AR 的标志性 demo。
highlights.note_en: Dial on your palm, play video on a newspaper, frame a photo with your fingers. The iconic demo of wearable projection AR.

highlights.note_zh: 一盏能移动、能投影、能识别桌面物体的台灯。把 AR 藏进日常家具里。
highlights.note_en: A lamp that moves, projects and recognizes objects on the desk. AR hidden inside everyday furniture.

highlights.note_zh: 把平板对准一个物理场景，AR 会预测并显示接下来会发生什么，比如物体会往哪里掉、往哪里滚。增强的是时间，而不只是空间。
highlights.note_en: Point a tablet at a physical scene and AR predicts what happens next — where things will fall or roll. It augments time, not only space.

highlights.note_zh: 用 HoloLens 在空中作画，并和真实环境融合。早期头显上的创作工具。
highlights.note_en: Painting in the air with HoloLens, blended with the real room. An early creation tool on headsets.

creators.tagline_en: Fingers and walls as the interface: wearable AR's first mass audience.
creators.intro_en: In 2009 Pranav Mistry, in Pattie Maes's MIT Fluid Interfaces group, showed SixthSense: a projector and camera worn around the neck let you operate information on your palm, a newspaper or a wall. The TED talk made the world imagine “AR you carry” for the first time.
creators.learn_en: How to demonstrate a big idea with the cheapest hardware (projector, camera, colored finger caps) and a story people understand.

creators.tagline_zh: 画一笔，现实就动起来：最新一代 AR 交互研究。
creators.intro_zh: Ryo Suzuki 在卡尔加里大学领导 Programmable Reality Lab，几乎每年都在 CHI 和 UIST 发表数篇 AR 交互论文。他的作品让手绘草图和真实世界的运动连接起来，特别适合教育和科学可视化。
creators.learn_zh: 学“动态草图”的思路：用户随手画的线不再是静态标注，而是会跟踪、测量、模拟的活参数。

highlights.note_zh: 在 AR 里画一条线，它就绑定到真实物体上，实时测量角度、生成图表。代表作。
highlights.note_en: Draw a line in AR and it binds to a real object, measuring angles and plotting graphs live. His signature work.

highlights.note_zh: 边讲话边自动生成相应的 AR 图形与关键词，演讲者不用准备幻灯片。
highlights.note_en: While you speak, matching AR graphics and keywords appear; the presenter needs no slides.

highlights.note_zh: 拍一下课本上的静态数学题，它就变成可以拖动、可以动起来的 AR 图形。
highlights.note_en: Point at a static math problem in a textbook and it becomes an AR figure you can drag and animate.

highlights.note_zh: 课本上的物理示意图被转换成可交互的模拟。AR 做教育的直接范例。
highlights.note_en: Physics diagrams from a textbook become interactive simulations. A direct example of AR for education.

creators.tagline_en: Draw a line and reality starts moving: the newest generation of AR interaction research.
creators.intro_en: Ryo Suzuki leads the Programmable Reality Lab at the University of Calgary and publishes several AR interaction papers at CHI and UIST nearly every year. His work links hand-drawn sketches to real-world motion, ideal for education and science visualization.
creators.learn_en: Dynamic sketching: a line the user draws is no longer a static annotation but a live parameter that tracks, measures and simulates.

creators.tagline_zh: 每周一个空间实验：2025–26 年 WebAR 与生成式世界的前沿。
creators.intro_zh: Ian Curtis（@XRarchitect）是建筑背景的设计师，先后在 8th Wall、Niantic 工作，现在在 World Labs。他在 X 上持续公开自己的实验，并写清楚用了什么工具。最近的方向是把 AI 生成的 3D 世界（Gaussian Splat）放进真实房间。
creators.learn_zh: 学“公开地快速原型”：新工具出来的当晚就做一个 demo，拍成 30 秒视频，写清楚技术栈。

highlights.note_zh: 8th Wall 的月球传送门：在街上打开一扇门，走进去就是月球。WebAR 传送门的范例。
highlights.note_en: 8th Wall's moon portal: open a door on the street and walk onto the moon. A model WebAR portal.

highlights.note_zh: AI 设计新客厅、生成 3D、再用 VPS 1:1 对齐到真实房间，人可以走进“重新设计后的家”。
highlights.note_en: AI designs a new living room, generates it in 3D, and VPS aligns it 1:1 to the real room so you can walk into the redesign.

highlights.note_zh: 用普通摄像头追踪人脸，让笔记本屏幕变成一扇有纵深的窗。不用头显的立体感。
highlights.note_en: A plain webcam tracks your face and turns a laptop screen into a window with depth. 3D without a headset.

highlights.note_zh: 把自己缩成手办大小，在茶几上的迷你世界里探险。尺度变换是最容易出惊喜的 AR 手法之一。
highlights.note_en: Shrink yourself to action-figure size and explore a tiny world on the coffee table. Changing scale is one of the most reliable sources of AR surprise.

highlights.note_zh: 两千万个 splat 组成的旧金山缩在桌上，手机一靠近就钻进街道。城市尺度的桌面 AR。
highlights.note_en: A 20-million-splat San Francisco on the table; move the phone closer and dive into the streets. City-scale tabletop AR.

creators.tagline_en: A spatial experiment every week: the 2025–26 frontier of WebAR and generated worlds.
creators.intro_en: Ian Curtis (@XRarchitect) is an architecture-trained designer who worked at 8th Wall and Niantic and is now at World Labs. He posts his experiments on X and lists exactly which tools he used. His recent direction: placing AI-generated 3D worlds (Gaussian splats) into real rooms.
creators.learn_en: Prototyping in public: build a demo the night a new tool ships, film 30 seconds, and write down the stack.

creators.tagline_zh: 跨越十几年、几乎每一代设备的 AR 实验者。
creators.intro_zh: 吉永崇（Takashi Yoshinaga）从 2009 年的医疗 AR 研究开始，一路在 Tango、ARCore、HoloLens、iPad LiDAR、Quest 3 上做原型，也是日本 AR 社区的重要教育者。他的实验常常用很巧妙的办法（比如借 YouTube 直播来传输全息影像）解决实际问题。
creators.learn_zh: 学“设备无关的点子”：同一个想法（复制现实、传送全息人）在每一代新硬件上重做一遍，看它怎么变好。

highlights.note_zh: 借用 YouTube 直播传输全息影像到手机 AR。用现成的基础设施解决难题，非常巧妙。
highlights.note_en: Holograms streamed to phone AR through YouTube Live. Solving a hard problem with existing infrastructure.

highlights.note_zh: 在 HoloLens 2 里框选一块真实房间“复制”成网格，再“粘贴”进另一个人手机的 ARCore 视图里。
highlights.note_en: Select a piece of the real room on HoloLens 2, “copy” it as a mesh, and “paste” it into another person's ARCore phone view.

highlights.note_zh: 追踪观看者的头部位置，让平面屏幕里的猫呈现正确的透视。和 Ian Curtis 的离轴投影可以对照着看。
highlights.note_en: Head tracking gives a cat on a flat screen correct perspective. Compare it with Ian Curtis's off-axis projection.

highlights.note_zh: 房间里一扇真实的门变成传送门：在 Quest 3 的透视画面中打开它，门后是一个虚拟世界。
highlights.note_en: A real door in the room becomes a portal: open it in Quest 3 passthrough and a virtual world is behind it.

highlights.note_zh: 在原地重放过去某一刻的人体动作，像空间里的时间回放。
highlights.note_en: Replay a past moment of human motion on the spot, like an instant replay in space.

creators.tagline_en: An AR experimenter across more than a decade and almost every device generation.
creators.intro_en: Takashi Yoshinaga began with medical AR research in 2009 and has since prototyped on Tango, ARCore, HoloLens, iPad LiDAR and Quest 3; he is also an important educator in Japan's AR community. His experiments often solve real problems with clever tricks, such as streaming holograms through YouTube Live.
creators.learn_en: Device-independent ideas: re-make the same idea (copying reality, sending a hologram of a person) on each new generation of hardware and see how it improves.

creators.tagline_zh: ARKit 早期最有想象力的一批原型，很多后来成了产品。
creators.intro_zh: Chris Laan 的 Laan Labs 在 2017 年 ARKit 发布后的几个月里，做出了一连串病毒式传播的 demo：AR 卷尺、空中喷漆、蟑螂满地爬……它们几乎定义了“手机 AR 能做什么”的早期想象，有些后来成了 App Store 上的热门应用。
creators.learn_zh: 学“一个 API 能力 = 一个点子”：平面检测、特征点、遮挡，每一种能力都可以直接变成一个好玩的小应用。

highlights.note_zh: AR 卷尺：最早证明手机 AR 实用价值的应用之一，后来苹果也内置了“测距仪”。
highlights.note_en: An AR tape measure: one of the first proofs that phone AR was useful. Apple later built in its own Measure app.

highlights.note_zh: 拿手机当喷漆罐，在墙上和空中涂鸦。空间绘画的大众版本。
highlights.note_en: Use the phone as a spray can to paint on walls and in the air. Spatial drawing for everyone.

highlights.note_zh: 一群蟑螂在真实的桌面和物体上爬。利用空间理解制造恐怖感，效果立竿见影。
highlights.note_en: A swarm of cockroaches crawls over real tables and objects. Spatial understanding used for instant horror.

highlights.note_zh: 2023 年：在手机上实时 AR 渲染 Gaussian Splat。从 2017 年的点云一路走到今天的新表示方式。
highlights.note_en: 2023: Gaussian splats rendered in real-time AR on a phone. From 2017 point clouds to today's new representation.

highlights.note_zh: 在 Vision Pro 上用手指直接在空中作画。同样的空间绘画点子，换到新设备上重做。
highlights.note_en: Finger-painting in the air on Vision Pro. The same spatial-drawing idea, re-made on a new device.

creators.tagline_en: The most imaginative early ARKit prototypes, several of which became products.
creators.intro_en: In the months after ARKit launched in 2017, Chris Laan's Laan Labs released a string of viral demos: an AR tape measure, spray paint in the air, cockroaches crawling everywhere. They defined the early picture of what phone AR could do, and some became hit apps.
creators.learn_en: One API capability = one idea: plane detection, feature points and occlusion can each become a small, playful app.

creators.name: Daito Manabe / Rhizomatiks
creators.tagline_zh: 把 AR 做成现场表演：舞者、无人机与混合现实舞台。
creators.intro_zh: 真锅大度（Daito Manabe）和 Rhizomatiks 团队与编舞家 MIKIKO、舞团 ELEVENPLAY 长期合作，把追踪、投影、无人机和 AR 转播结合成现场演出，从 Perfume 的舞台一直做到里约奥运会闭幕式上的东京八分钟。他们的作品覆盖了本库最多的交互类型。
creators.learn_zh: 学把 AR 当“现场媒介”：一切都必须实时、零失误，而且要同时服务现场观众和屏幕前的观众。

highlights.note_zh: 三位舞者和 24 架发光无人机同台，无人机组成的光点阵形随编舞变化，框住舞者的动作。
highlights.note_en: Three dancers and 24 glowing drones share the stage; the drones' formations of light shift with the choreography and frame the dancers.

highlights.note_zh: 观众坐在自动移动的轮椅上戴着头显，看到的真实舞者和虚拟舞者无缝混合。混合现实舞台的代表作。
highlights.note_en: Audience members ride automated wheelchairs wearing headsets; real and virtual dancers merge seamlessly. The signature mixed-reality stage.

highlights.note_zh: 击剑剑尖的轨迹被实时追踪并画在电视转播画面上。AR 让观众看懂一项太快的运动。
highlights.note_en: The tips of fencing blades are tracked and drawn on the TV broadcast in real time. AR helps viewers follow a sport too fast to see.

highlights.note_zh: 与 Kyle McDonald 合作：机器学习生成的虚拟舞者和真人同台。
highlights.note_en: With Kyle McDonald: machine-learning-generated virtual dancers share the stage with real ones.

highlights.note_zh: border 的 2021 新版，可以和 2015 年的原版对比，看技术进步如何改变同一个作品。
highlights.note_en: The 2021 version of border. Compare it with 2015 to see how technology changes the same work.

creators.tagline_en: AR as live performance: dancers, drones and mixed-reality stages.
creators.intro_en: Daito Manabe and Rhizomatiks work with choreographer MIKIKO and the dance company ELEVENPLAY, combining tracking, projection, drones and AR broadcast into live shows — from Perfume's stages to the Tokyo segment of the Rio 2016 closing ceremony. Their work covers more interaction types than any other creator here.
creators.learn_en: AR as a live medium: everything must run in real time with zero failures, for the audience in the room and the one watching on screens.

creators.tagline_zh: AR 未来的批判性想象：HYPER-REALITY 的作者。
creators.intro_zh: 松田圭一（Keiichi Matsuda）是建筑师出身的设计师兼导演。2016 年的短片《HYPER-REALITY》描绘了一个被广告和界面淹没的 AR 城市，至今仍是讨论 AR 伦理最常被引用的作品。他曾在 Leap Motion 负责设计，现在的工作室 Liquid City 在做空间 AI 智能体。
creators.learn_zh: 学“设计虚构”：用一段短片来想象和批判一种尚不存在的未来，而不只是做一个能用的 demo。

highlights.note_zh: 2010 年的研究生作品：厨房里的每件物品都贴满界面。HYPER-REALITY 的雏形。
highlights.note_en: A 2010 graduate project: every object in a kitchen is covered in interfaces. The seed of HYPER-REALITY.

highlights.note_zh: 必看。广告、游戏化、身份系统把整座城市淹没。适合作为 AR 伦理讨论课的开场。
highlights.note_en: Essential viewing: ads, gamification and identity systems flood a whole city. A strong opener for a class on AR ethics.

highlights.note_zh: 一个在 AR 里全天候工作的人，与机器的边界逐渐模糊。“AR 办公”的暗面。
highlights.note_en: A worker who spends all day in AR, the line between her and the machine blurring. The dark side of “AR at work”.

highlights.note_zh: Liquid City 的短片：AI 智能体以角色形象出现在 AR 眼镜里，替主人公协商安排一天。从批判走向追问：我们想和 AI 建立什么关系？
highlights.note_en: A Liquid City short: AI agents appear as characters in AR glasses and negotiate the protagonist's day. From critique to the question: what relationship do we want with AI?

creators.tagline_en: A critical imagination of AR's future: the author of HYPER-REALITY.
creators.intro_en: Keiichi Matsuda is an architecture-trained designer and director. His 2016 short HYPER-REALITY shows a city drowned in ads and interfaces and is still the most-cited work in debates about AR ethics. He led design at Leap Motion; his studio Liquid City now builds spatial AI agents.
creators.learn_en: Design fiction: use a short film to imagine and critique a future that does not exist yet, rather than only building a working demo.

creators.tagline_zh: 公共空间里的身体、影子与投影：“关系建筑”系列。
creators.intro_zh: Rafael Lozano-Hemmer 从 1990 年代开始在城市广场做巨型互动投影，他称之为“关系建筑”（Relational Architecture）：让路人的影子、心跳和声音改写建筑的表面。他证明了不需要任何个人设备，也能让成千上万人一起“增强”一个空间。
creators.learn_zh: 学公共空间的 AR：没有 App、没有头显，任何路过的人都能成为作品的一部分。

highlights.note_zh: 路人的影子投到建筑上，影子里会露出其他人的肖像。公共投影 AR 的里程碑。
highlights.note_en: Passers-by's shadows fall on a building and reveal portraits of other people inside them. A milestone of public projection AR.

highlights.note_zh: 广场被白光照亮，行人的影子里浮现出本地居民的视频肖像，他们抬头看你，在你离开时消失。
highlights.note_en: A square flooded with white light; video portraits of local people appear in pedestrians' shadows, look up at them, and vanish when they leave.

highlights.note_zh: 进入房间的每个人身上都被投上一个随机的动词，而且会跟着他移动。给人贴标签，是追踪技术的隐喻。
highlights.note_en: Each person entering the room gets a random verb projected on their body, following them around. Labeling people as a metaphor for tracking technology.

highlights.note_zh: 人脸识别摄像头把观众之间的关系放大投射到墙上。监控技术的艺术化呈现。
highlights.note_en: Face-detecting cameras amplify the relationships between visitors onto the walls. Surveillance technology made into art.

creators.tagline_en: Bodies, shadows and projection in public space: the “Relational Architecture” series.
creators.intro_en: Since the 1990s Rafael Lozano-Hemmer has staged huge interactive projections in city squares, which he calls Relational Architecture: passers-by's shadows, heartbeats and voices rewrite the surface of buildings. He showed that thousands of people can augment a space together without any personal device.
creators.learn_en: AR in public space: no app, no headset — anyone walking by becomes part of the work.

creators.tagline_zh: 镜像式互动与动态形态：视觉语言最强的数字艺术工作室。
creators.intro_zh: Matt Pyke 在英国谢菲尔德创立的 Universal Everything，以“会动的人形”闻名：用动作捕捉驱动千变万化的角色。他们的互动作品大多是“魔镜”：你一动，镜子里的另一个你就跟着变形。
creators.learn_zh: 学“视觉风格就是交互”：同样是一个身体追踪，形态设计决定了人们愿不愿意在镜子前停留、起舞。

highlights.note_zh: Barbican 的动作捕捉镜子：每位观众都变成一个合成的机器人形象，你动得越用力，它的反应越奇异（共有 4.7 万种可能）。
highlights.note_en: A motion-capture mirror at the Barbican: every visitor becomes a synthetic robotic figure, and the harder you move the stranger it gets (47,000 possible responses).

highlights.note_zh: 把他们的动态角色做成手机 AR App，让普通人也能召唤出巨大的“超级自己”。
highlights.note_en: Their moving characters as a phone AR app, so anyone can summon a giant “super self”.

highlights.note_zh: 用 LiDAR 理解真实空间，让抽象的数字生命在你的房间里生长。
highlights.note_en: LiDAR understands the real room so abstract digital life can grow inside it.

highlights.note_zh: AR 建筑：抬头看城市的天际线，建筑之上叠加出新的动态结构。
highlights.note_en: AR architecture: look up at the skyline and new moving structures appear on top of buildings.

highlights.note_zh: 一个会模仿路人动作和外表的数字生命，出现在东伦敦的街头屏幕上，后来又去了威尼斯和北京。公共空间版本的魔镜。
highlights.note_en: A digital being that imitates passers-by's movement and appearance on street screens in East London, later Venice and Beijing. The magic mirror in public space.

creators.tagline_en: Mirror-like interaction and moving form: the digital art studio with the strongest visual language.
creators.intro_en: Universal Everything, founded by Matt Pyke in Sheffield, is known for moving human figures: motion capture driving endlessly varied characters. Most of their interactive works are magic mirrors — you move, and another version of you transforms in the glass.
creators.learn_en: Visual style is interaction: with the same body tracking, the form design decides whether people stop and dance in front of the mirror.
